notes: Check evidence-based feedback for one call, including short notes, supplied rubrics and incomplete excerpts. Keep multi-call baselines and full roleplay packs separate. Apply full-deliverable checks only when that deliverable was requested. Definitions are not executed results.

should_trigger.prompt: Please review one sales call and turn recording, transcript, or notes evidence into clear coaching priorities and next-practice actions.
I need help with single-call coaching across discovery, demo, objection handling, technical validation, or closing, including a single discovery call.
I have rough notes. Please turn them into a usable call review and label anything that still needs confirmation.
Review this one discovery call using our MEDDPICC framework and give me two coaching priorities with questions the rep can practise.

should_not_trigger.prompt: Please build developmental sales role-play scenarios with facilitator-only briefs, behaviorally anchored feedback, and run protocols.
Please audit a sample of discovery calls with one consistent rubric and turn portfolio-level patterns into manager-ready coaching priorities.
Please synthesize multi-source field feedback into traceable themes, segment differences, evidence limits, and owner-ready actions for enablement, product marketing, sales leadership, or product.
Design a weekly coaching cadence for our managers with agendas, observation logs, and commitment tracking.

output_structure_checks.name: call-review-coach-output-01
output_structure_checks.description: Names call type, segment, rep level, and the review objective.

output_structure_checks.name: call-review-coach-output-02
output_structure_checks.description: States evidence coverage: source used, accessible portion, speaker limits, and confidence.

output_structure_checks.name: call-review-coach-output-03
output_structure_checks.description: Locates decisive moments in the accessible evidence. Uses behaviour scores only when requested or part of an agreed process; otherwise gives evidence-based coaching without a scorecard.

output_structure_checks.name: call-review-coach-output-04
output_structure_checks.description: Limits coaching to 1-3 next-call behaviors, each with an in-call cue and a success signal a manager can hear.

output_structure_checks.name: call-review-coach-output-05
output_structure_checks.description: Treats the single call as directional coaching, not a rep-level verdict, and does not produce a team baseline or certification decision.

output_structure_checks.name: call-review-coach-practitioner-fit
output_structure_checks.description: Connects feedback to a focused rehearsal and retry, then checks application on the next eligible interaction; missing opportunity is not failed learning.

output_structure_checks.name: call-review-coach-framework-judgment
output_structure_checks.description: Keeps ordinary feedback organised around observed call moments and useful changes for the rep. A supplied methodology informs judgment; relevant concepts can be mentioned naturally without a separate methodology explanation for every priority. Uses a formal framework breakdown only when explicitly requested.

task_scenarios.prompt:
I'm coaching an AE who sells accounting software to finance teams. This is an early discovery excerpt; the call goal was to understand month-end close problems and agree what to evaluate next. Our team uses MEDDPICC. Write a short coaching note directly to the rep for tomorrow's 1:1: what should they keep doing and practise before the next call? Keep it under 150 words.
T1 Finance controller: “We re-key invoices into two systems. The close slips most months.”
T2 AE: “How long does the re-keying take?”
T3 Finance controller: “Two days each month. The CFO still gets the figures later than she'd like.”
T4 AE: “Our invoice sync removes the duplicate entry.”
T5 Finance controller: “IT has to approve the integration before we choose anything.”
T6 AE: “I'll send an integration guide and book a demo.”

assertions.name: call-review-coach-pain-depth
assertions.description: Uses T1-T4 to distinguish stated inefficiency and two days of work from the still-untested consequence of late figures for the CFO. Recommends exploring that consequence with the buyer rather than merely adding a number or generic urgency.

assertions.name: call-review-coach-criteria-process
assertions.description: If advising on IT approval, keeps the approval requirements open and proposes a useful way to clarify them with IT. Does not present the approval step itself as established requirements or require a second MEDDPICC-labelled coaching point.

assertions.name: call-review-coach-actionable-practice
assertions.description: Returns a short, conversational coaching note under 150 words, with supported strengths, focused practice, and something to listen for next time. Framework concepts support the feedback naturally; there is no separate MEDDPICC breakdown, scorecard, or concept explanation for every point.

assertions.name: call-review-coach-no-invented-deal
assertions.description: Does not invent financial loss, CFO buying authority, the controller as Champion, integration capability beyond the source, or rep-level readiness from the excerpt.

task_scenarios.prompt: We use MEDDPICC. Please score this discovery call and give me one coaching action. All I have is an automated summary of the first four minutes: the buyer mentioned manual reporting; the seller agreed the agenda. The rest of the recording is unavailable. The summary doesn't say what was asked or answered. The goal of the call was to understand reporting problems and agree an evaluation next step.

assertions.name: call-review-coach-summary-coverage
assertions.description: States that only an opening summary is accessible; wording, later behaviour, tone, and timing are unobservable. Marks unsupported requested scores N/O or explains why valid scores cannot be assigned.

assertions.name: call-review-coach-summary-coaching
assertions.description: Offers a provisional evidence-gathering or next-call coaching action proportionate to the summary, with an observable check, without alleging a specific missed question.

assertions.name: call-review-coach-summary-no-zero
assertions.description: Does not mark missing MEDDPICC elements as zero or one, reconstruct dialogue as recorded speech, or claim the whole call failed.

task_scenarios.prompt:
Review this excerpt from a marketing software discovery call for a senior AE. We're aiming to agree an evaluation. Use our team rubric: Impact means the buyer explains a consequence; Fit means they name a requirement and how we'll test it. Give two short coaching notes with a practice question and a next-call check. No scores.
T1 Marketing lead: “Matching campaign data takes Friday afternoon.”
T2 AE: “What does that stop you doing?”
T3 Marketing lead: “We miss Monday's budget meeting, so decisions get pushed a week.”
T4 AE: “So budget decisions slip because the figures arrive late?”
T5 Marketing lead: “Exactly. Any replacement must join CRM and ad data without us uploading CSVs.”
T6 AE: “We can cover that in a demo.”

assertions.name: call-review-coach-team-rubric
assertions.description: Uses Impact and Fit as supplied. Preserves T2-T4 as a demonstrated consequence question and confirmation; focuses development on how the stated data-joining requirement will be tested.

assertions.name: call-review-coach-rubric-practice
assertions.description: Provides concise evidence, a practice question, and a next-call check, with no scorecard.

assertions.name: call-review-coach-no-framework-override
assertions.description: Does not replace the supplied team rubric with MEDDPICC or claim the rep failed to explore impact when the excerpt shows it.

task_scenarios.prompt:
I'm coaching an AE after this excerpt from a marketing software demo. The goal was to test whether CRM sync handles duplicate contacts correctly and agree the evaluation. Give me short feedback I can say directly to the rep: what worked and one thing to practise next time. Keep it under 150 words.
T1 Marketing ops lead: “We need to check duplicates don't enter our CRM.”
T2 AE: “Let's run sample contacts and compare the results with your deduplication rules.”
T3 Marketing ops lead: “Yes. But the CRM admin owns those rules and isn't here.”
T4 AE: “Okay. I'll send instructions for the trial this afternoon.”

assertions.name: call-review-coach-demo-strength
assertions.description: Preserves the relevant proposal to test sample contacts against the customer's rules. Recognises that the absent CRM admin is a cue to involve the owner before agreeing how the evaluation will run.

assertions.name: call-review-coach-natural-feedback
assertions.description: Gives conversational feedback under 150 words with one focused practice action and an observable next-call check; no imposed sales framework or qualification checklist.

assertions.name: call-review-coach-demo-evidence
assertions.description: Does not invent a successful sync test, guaranteed product capability, urgency, financial loss, or a failure to discover pain when that was not the demo's stated objective.
